Btec Level 1 Introductory Science
BTEC Applied Science at RVC aims to develop both transferable and sector skills. This is important as it helps progression to further study – whether that be to other BTECs, to apprenticeships or to training. The curriculum is designed in a way that means there is flexibility so that units can be selected to meet the needs of the learners. All of the units offer different aspects of Science therefore ensuring a broad and balanced curriculum. We intend for every learner to have the opportunity to develop key transferable skills through both core and sector units. This will help learners to appreciate how the transferable skills they develop in their core units can be contextualised in the sector they are studying. On completion of their course, learners will have developed a set of transferable and sector skills that will benefit them whatever their chosen progression route.
The nature of the assessments means all learners will build confidence in IT skills due to how their coursework is presented. Applied Science results in all learners gaining experience in coursework based assessment which encourages improved organisational and presenting skills. Learners will be able to participate in practical assessments where they develop their problem solving skills.This course offers achievable assessments allowing students to building confidence by achieving a qualification.

GCSE Citizenship
To Develop knowledge, skills and understanding that pupils need to play a full part in a democratic society, as active and informed citizens. Challenging stereotypes and preconceived prejudices gives students information to play a positive and educated role in society. Pupils are taught about democracy, politics, parliament and voting. Pupils will learn to have and develop opinions of their own about the world in which they live and the current affairs that affect them and their communities. Additionally they learn about human rights, justice, the law, identities and diversity
At RVC we implement our curriculum through a range of teaching approaches including role play, games/ quizzes and creative tasks as well as more traditional information sharing with questions and essay writing. Discussion and debate are a regular feature of lessons, as well as regular assessment for learning to ensure key content is secure.
Students will leave with a greater confidence and attitude to participate in Society in a positive way. Students will make well informed opinions about the world we live in. Stereotypes will be challenged and students will question their preconceived prejudices.

GCSE English
At Reigate Valley College, our aim is to support students to initially engage in the subject. Due to previous trauma from mainstream experiences). Delivering a diverse, captivating and flexible English curriculum which is tailored to the needs of our students. To support students in developing a positive mindset towards the different aspects of the subject and to recognise where they excel.
We are flexible in our curriculum content and offer, using adaptive teaching and learning, in response to the individual learning needs. We use regular CAT tests and reading age assessments to identify gaps that need addressing. We have a consistent assessment and feedback cycle and regularly practice of tier 2 and subject specific vocab.
Students leave RVC with a positive mindset towards English. They have developed resilience, confidence and the ability to take calculated risk. Students have a wider knowledge base. Students leave with a qualification specific to their personalised learning plan. (AQA Entry level, Functional Skills/ GCSE)

Meet the Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section.
At Reigate Valley College, a Pupil Referral Unit and academy dedicated to providing an inclusive, high-quality education for students aged 5 to 16, governance plays a vital role in ensuring our school thrives and delivers on its mission. Our Local Governing Body (LGB) is a committed team of individuals who meet three times a year to oversee the strategic direction and accountability of the school. This page introduces you to the crucial role our governors play in supporting our vision and values.
The Role of the Local Governing Body
The LGB at Reigate Valley College is central to maintaining our culture of honesty, respect, and compassion. Governors work collaboratively with the Head of School, staff, parents, and the wider community to:
Governors bring a wealth of experience from diverse backgrounds, enabling them to provide well-rounded guidance and challenge that benefits our students and staff alike.
How Governance Supports Our Vision and Values
Our governors embody the core values of Reigate Valley College by:
By supporting supportive collaboration between the school, families, and partner organisations, governors help us create an environment where students feel seen, valued, and empowered to reach their potential.

SEND
At Reigate Valley College, we are committed to ensuring that our students feel safe and happy in school so that they can build positive relationships and have the ability to approach their learning confidently and successfully. However, we recognise that, for some of our students, their educational journey that has led them to RVC may have been challenging and they may find the demands of a busy school environment difficult to manage, leaving them struggling to cope with their emotions and anxieties. We acknowledge that behaviour is a form of communication, that we have a duty to discover what the behaviour is telling us and to support our students to develop the skills to communicate effectively.
For the majority of our students, good, inclusive classroom practice and positive behaviour management strategies will provide the support needed. But for others, a more tailored approach and additional intervention may be needed. We aim to provide our most vulnerable students with safe, calm spaces and skilled, experienced staff. We strive to offer an inclusive education that caters for the needs of all students. All staff demonstrate inclusive practice implementing strategies and methods that ensure all learners can access education. We endeavour to ensure that all learners feel valued and supported and their individual needs are recognised and met. Our personalised provision has been deliberately designed to support the needs of our students, whether or not additional needs have been identified. A stable and predictable daily routine, which focuses on developmentally appropriate activities, helps them to recognise, communicate and regulate their emotions. Through this carefully targeted and sensitive support, we enable children and young people to build trusting and secure relationships with adults and a sense of self-worth. We also work in constant partnership with both the Local Authority and our network of schools in order to establish the best outcomes for our students both when they join us but also when they transition on to their next provision in order to make this a successful and positive experience for them. The aim is that this allows them to experience success in the classroom and beyond, avoiding the potential long-term consequences of educational disengagement.
Some of our students may need more than the inclusive strategies implemented daily in our classrooms. At RVC, we therefore use the Graduated Approach to support our students. An effective Graduated Approach draws on more detailed approaches, more frequent review and more specialist expertise in successive cycles in order to match interventions to an individual child or young person's needs. The SEND Code of Practice states that, for these learners, teachers are required to remove barriers to learning and put effective special educational provision in place through SEN support. This SEN support takes the form of a four-part cycle (assess, plan, do, review). Through this cycle, actions are reviewed and refined as understanding of a student’s needs and the support required to help them secure good outcomes increases. Students who continue to face challenges in their learning, despite receiving high-quality teaching, are likely to need additional strategies, or different provision, in order to meet their needs. In these circumstances, the Graduated Approach will be used to request statutory assessment to see if a student requires an Education, Health and Care Plan.
Contact can be made to our SEN team via email srebbeck@ietmat.co.uk
Please click to visit the IET website for our SEND policy

Curriculum
The focus of the curriculum is to ensure that every student is able to develop their learning and associated strategies to succeed in the classroom at the Phoenix Campus and then onto their next educational establishment. The pupils often arrive with barriers to their learning which, over time are addressed by staff in an attempt to create an optimum learning environment for them to begin to experience success.
Every pupil has a Key Worker who they will meet on a weekly basis to discuss areas of achievement and difficulties as well as agreeing appropriate targets going forward. ELSA lessons are delivered to address vital learning such as emotional regulation, relationships, safety (including online safety), managing feelings and conflict.
The out of lesson learning is considered to be equally as important as time in front of a teacher. These are the opportunities for the children to experience and learn from situations they normally face with great difficulty. These will often present themselves in the playground with friendship issues, challenging game situations or conflict.
It is this overall curriculum package that underpins the academic and pastoral development of each child within the Phoenix. This in turn provides the basis for the potential continuation of this improvement within their next school.
Mon - Thurs Arrive 9:00am; depart 2:00pm (5 hours per day)
Friday Arrive 9:00am; depart 1.30pm (4 1/2 hours each Friday)
All break and lunch periods are fully staffed and aimed at building relationships, addressing / modelling behaviour and encouraging positive interaction between peers.

Curriculum
The focus of the curriculum is to ensure that the every student is given the skills to succeed in an ever changing world. It is recognised that our out of lesson learning is equally as important as the time in front of a teacher.
Every student has a mentor who is responsible for ensuring good behaviour and good pastoral development outside of lessons. At break and lunch all members of the Pastoral Care Team are present to be role models, demonstrate how to interact and engage in a variety of situations, discuss and help remove those barriers to progress.
To gain an all-round experience at school, students also follow core subjects and option choices. On Thursday's pupils follow a more vocational timetable giving them more options to choose. On Fridays pupils have the opportunity to develop further through a selection of enrichment activities.
Pupils can also use Thursdays and Fridays to go to work experience placements to help best prepare them for the world of work.
It is the balance of pastoral and academic development which has seen RVC students achieve so much success, which then underpins the strategies to succeed back in their mainstream school and post 16.

Careers
At Reigate Valley College we are committed to providing all students with meaningful and appropriate Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) regarding education pathways at post 16, apprenticeships and careers. IAG is delivered through the curriculum and in 1:1 sessions. Assistance is given to students in applying for post 16 pathways. This support is extended once students have left at the end of Year 11 to ensure a smooth transition.
The websites below may also be useful:
Careerometer can be used to explore and compare key information about occupations, help you learn about different occupations and identify potential careers. It provides access to a selection of UK headline data relating to pay, weekly hours of work and future employment prospects for different occupations, as well as description of the occupation. Simply type in the title of the job you are interested in and the widget provides a series of options from which you can select the most relevant to you. You can then look up another two occupations and compare. You can also select ‘display the UK average’ and compare the information with the occupation you have selected
Skillsometer can help you discover what jobs you might like to do in the future. You will be presented with a series of statements. Select the emoji shows how you feel about each statement. You will then be given suggestions of jobs linked to what you most enjoy doing. For each job, you will be presented with some headline UK data.
The National Careers Service provides information, advice and guidance to help you make decisions on learning, training and work opportunities. The service offers confidential and impartial advice. This is supported by qualified careers advisers.

Careersbox is a free online library of careers related film, news and information. As the preferred digital new media partner to the Institute of Career Guidance, the largest careers body in the UK, Careersbox aim is to deliver a new way for students to explore their skills and career options.
LifeSkills, created with Barclays, is a free, curriculum-linked programme, developed with teachers to help improve the skills and employability of young people in the UK.
icould has a range of video clips showing real people talking about their jobs and careers.
Your choices at 14, 16 and 18, explore different job sectors and how you can study and work at the same time - even to university level
The place for young people to explore careers, get the lowdown on top employers, and search for the latest jobs, courses and advice.
